explanation: Biblical patriarch and ancestor of the people of Israel, whom God chose to make a covenant with.
Abraham's son, born to his wife Sarah. Isaac is a central figure in Genesis and is regarded as one of the patriarchs in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
A holy act in which something is given to God, often as a symbolic gesture to show gratitude, devotion, or obedience.
A mountain region mentioned in Genesis 22, where Abraham was asked to sacrifice his son Isaac as a sign of his faith and obedience to God.
A supernatural being who serves as God's messenger and servant. In this story, an angel stops Abraham from sacrificing Isaac and shows him an alternative offering.
A male sheep found by Abraham and sacrificed in place of Isaac after the angel intervened.
An agreement between God and people, often connected with promises and conditions. In this case, God confirms his covenant with Abraham and promises to bless him and his descendants.
